name: outsb
synopsis: void outsb(unsigned short port, const void *addr, unsigned long count);
description: outsb is used to output a string of bytes from a memory buffer to the specified I/O port. It performs low-level port output operations and is primarily intended for internal kernel use but can be accessed from user space with proper permissions.

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The I/O port to which the data will be output.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Pointer to the memory buffer containing the data to output.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number of bytes to output from the buffer.

return_value.success: No return value; function completes successfully.
return_value.failure: May cause a segmentation fault if I/O permissions are not set via ioperm(2) or iopl(2).

bugs: Functions require compilation with optimization flags like -O or -O2, as they are defined as inline macros; hardware-specific and may differ from other implementations, such as DOS.
